q: What is the average cost of `x in s` when `s` is a Python set?
why: The hash picks the bucket directly. On average buckets hold very few keys, so the check is O(1).

q: What is the time complexity of this loop?
why: `x in seen` on a list scans it: O(n) per check, O(n²) overall. Making `seen` a set brings it down to O(n).

q: When can a hash table lookup cost O(n)?
options: When many keys land in the same bucket
why: If most keys collide into one bucket, a lookup has to walk that whole chain. Good hash functions and resizing make this rare.

q: In one-pass Two Sum, why check `target - x in index` before storing `x`?
options: So x can't pair with itself
Dicts can't be updated inside a loop
why: If x were stored first, target = 2x would find x itself, e.g. [3, 2, 4] with target 6 would return [0, 0].

q: Which clue most strongly suggests a hash map?
options: You need to repeatedly ask "have I seen this value?"
You need the k-th smallest element
why: Repeated membership or lookup questions are exactly what hash maps make O(1).
